steps.title: Download SRA data and create FASTQ.gz files
steps.instruction: Use SRA‑Toolkit (v3.1.0) to prefetch all listed SRR run IDs, extract FASTQ files with fasterq‑dump (50 threads), and compress the resulting FASTQ files to .fastq.gz using gzip.

steps.title: Initial quality assessment of raw reads
steps.instruction: Run FastQC on all compressed FASTQ files using 10 threads and combine the individual HTML reports with MultiQC.

steps.title: Trim adapters and filter low‑quality bases
steps.instruction: Trim adapters and low‑quality bases from both paired‑end and single‑end reads using TrimGalore (quality 20, stringency 7, retain_unpaired for PE, 2 cores) and/or fastp (v0.23.4, 16 threads, detect adapters, cut tail, correction, over‑representation analysis). After trimming, re‑run FastQC and MultiQC to verify quality.

substeps.instruction: $ fastp -i SRR18042662_1.fastq.gz -I SRR18042662_2.fastq.gz -o SRR18042662_1_clean.fastq.gz -O SRR18042662_2_clean.fastq.gz --detect_adapter_for_pe --cut_tail --correction --overrepresentation_analysis --json SRR18042662.fastp.json --html SRR18042662.fastp.html --thread 16

steps.title: Build genome indexes for host and pathogen
steps.instruction: Create a HISAT2 index for the human hg38 genome (including splice‑site and exon files), a BWA index for the Mycobacterium tuberculosis genome, and optionally a STAR index for hg38.

steps.title: Map reads to host and pathogen genomes (choose approach)
steps.instruction: Two alternative strategies are provided. (A) Host‑first: map trimmed reads to hg38 with HISAT2, extract unmapped reads, then map those to the Mtb genome with BWA. (B) Pathogen‑first: map trimmed reads to the Mtb genome with BWA, extract unmapped reads, then map those to hg38 with HISAT2. Use samtools and bedtools to convert between BAM and FASTQ as needed.

substeps.instruction: $ hisat2 --dta -x hisat2_hg38_index/hg38_index -1 2.Trimmed_reads/SRR18042662_trimmed_1.fq.gz -2 2.Trimmed_reads/SRR18042662_trimmed_2.fq.gz -p 20 --un-conc-gz B.Mapping_HISAT2/SRR18042662_Unmapped_pairs --summary-file B.Mapping_HISAT2/SRR18042662_align_stats.txt | samtools view -@15 -b -S | samtools sort -n -@15 -o B.Mapping_HISAT2/SRR18042662.sorted.bam -O BAM

$ hisat2 --dta -x hisat2_hg38_index/hg38_index -U 2.Trimmed_reads/SRR18042663_trimmed.fq.gz -p 20 --un-conc-gz B.Mapping_HISAT2/SRR18042663_Unmapped_reads.fq.gz --summary-file B.Mapping_HISAT2/SRR18042663_align_stats.txt | samtools view -@15 -b -S | samtools sort -n -@15 -o B.Mapping_HISAT2/SRR18042663.sorted.bam -O BAM
# Extract unmapped reads (host‑first) from the HISAT2 BAM files
# BWA mapping of unmapped reads to Mtb genome (paired‑end)

$ bwa mem -t 20 GCF_000195955.2_ASM19595v2_genomic.fna B.Mapping_HISAT2/SRR18042662_unmapped_1.fq B.Mapping_HISAT2/SRR18042662_unmapped_2.fq | samtools view -@15 -b -S | samtools sort -n -@15 -o B.Mapping_BWA_HostFirst/SRR18042662_Mtb.bam -O BAM

$ bwa mem -t 20 GCF_000195955.2_ASM19595v2_genomic.fna 2.Trimmed_reads/SRR18042663_trimmed.fq.gz | samtools view -@15 -b -S | samtools sort -n -@15 -o B.Mapping_BWA_PathogenFirst/SRR18042663.sorted.bam -O BAM

steps.title: Quantify gene‑level read counts
steps.instruction: Use featureCounts to count reads mapping to exonic regions of the Mtb and hg38 annotations for both paired‑end and single‑end BAM files, then merge the paired‑ and single‑end count tables.

steps.title: Differential expression and functional enrichment
steps.instruction: Import the merged count matrices into DESeq2, edgeR or Cuffdiff for differential gene expression analysis. Perform Gene Ontology and pathway enrichment with BINGO, CytoHubba, and DAVID. Optionally annotate differentially expressed genes using BLAST against external databases.

description: Validation of protocol The number of reads retained after each step in the analysis significantly impacts data quality, especially when dealing with a dataset containing reads from multiple species. In this protocol, we have identified and listed the top-performing software predominantly used for such analyses. Additionally, we have tabulated the results obtained at each step after thoroughly benchmarking these software tools. Besides the software chosen for trimming and mapping in this protocol, the other sections were validated in earlier studies, which include mapping strategy [10] and choice of genome annotation [17].
